cards.name: fxTechnicolor(3strip)
cards.summary: Not a usable colour LUT on its own: it is the 3D texture behind SpeedGrade's 'Technicolor 3-strip' film shader (fxTechnicolor(3strip).irtp in the same folder). Read as a plain LUT it brightens about 1.25x and turns any pixel above ~77% in any channel black.
use_for: Do not apply; for a 3-strip Technicolor feel build it manually (saturated primaries, warm reds, deep greens) with Lumetri HSL / saturation
Reference only: Premiere ships the SpeedGrade film shaders without exposing them
avoid: Applying it via Look > Browse: highlights go black
Treating the .lut file as a standard Technicolor emulation LUT
cards.scripting: Measured: the file is .cube-format text (TITLE 'Technicolor 3strip LUT', LUT_3D_SIZE 32) holding a 25-point colour cube padded to 32 (indices 25-31 are all zero), consumed by the .irtp shader with its own coordinate scaling; Premiere does not expose .irtp film shaders, and the .lut extension may not even be accepted by Browse. Selecting a LUT file from a spec is not possible: in Premiere the Lumetri Color properties 'Look' (0-68) and 'Input LUT' (0-11) are popup indices (0 = None) with undocumented, install-dependent ordering, 'LookAsset' / 'LUTAsset' are file blobs a spec cannot set, and the Lumetri Presets store older legacy indices that must not be copied either. Practical routes: in Premiere apply the Lumetri preset or Browse by hand (AdobeBridge's Premiere build cannot apply effect presets), or set the index on a probe clip and verify with a rendered frame; in AE (same file under Support Files/Lumetri) load it once through Lumetri Color's Browse or Apply Color LUT, save an animation preset (.ffx) and apply that from the spec's 'presets' (check a render that the LUT came along).

Selecting a LUT file from a spec is not possible: in Premiere the Lumetri Color properties 'Look' (0-68) and 'Input LUT' (0-11) are popup indices (0 = None) with undocumented, install-dependent ordering, 'LookAsset' / 'LUTAsset' are file blobs a spec cannot set, and the Lumetri Presets store older legacy indices that must not be copied either. Practical routes: in Premiere apply the Lumetri preset or Browse by hand (AdobeBridge's Premiere build cannot apply effect presets), or set the index on a probe clip and verify with a rendered frame; in AE (same file under Support Files/Lumetri) load it once through Lumetri Color's Browse or Apply Color LUT, save an animation preset (.ffx) and apply that from the spec's 'presets' (check a render that the LUT came along).
